note: Screen corpus for the pane-state evaluator. Every case is upstream's OWN test screen and expected answer, lifted from herdr src/detect/manifest/tests.rs at commit 6f311498aeeb27c0973781961ef94e8d0016ed17. Running them through this Go port is a CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION parity check, not a self-consistency one: the screens and the answers both come from the reference implementation. Tests that install a synthetic or remote manifest are excluded. Each case's expected rule is read only from the assertions BEFORE the next explain() call in the same test function — reading further attributed one screen's rule id to another. These are observations; regenerating is manual. Review pass 2026-08-08: extended to EVERY eligible test in that file (28 cases) — the first cut omitted the multi-signal cases (blocker-outranks-working, transcript-viewer freeze, OSC-vs-screen preference), which are exactly where a port divergence would matter most.
